qe: Prior to the systematic structural changes introduced during British rule, what was the primary unit of judicial administration for the Muslim population at the local level?
qh: ब्रिटिश शासन द्वारा शुरू किए गए व्यवस्थित संरचनात्मक परिवर्तनों से पहले, स्थानीय स्तर पर मुस्लिम आबादी के लिए न्यायिक प्रशासन की प्राथमिक इकाई क्या थी?
o: The office of the Qazi
The District Fauzdari Court
The Sadar Nizamat Assembly
The Mufti Circuit Council
e: Detailed Explanation: In pre-colonial and Mughal times, the unit of local judicial administration for Muslims was the office of the Qazi. These religious officers were located in provincial capitals, towns, and qasbas (large villages) to dispense justice based on Islamic law.

qe: The historical genesis of a common law system based on recorded judicial precedents in India can be traced back to the formal establishment of Mayor's Courts in 1726 in which presidencies?
qh: भारत में दर्ज न्यायिक मिसालों (judicial precedents) पर आधारित सामान्य कानून व्यवस्था की ऐतिहासिक शुरुआत 1726 में किन प्रेसीडेंसियों में मेयर कोर्ट की औपचारिक स्थापना से मानी जा सकती है?
o: Madras, Bombay, and Calcutta
Calcutta, Dacca, and Murshidabad
Madras, Patna, and Allahabad
Bombay, Surat, and Masulipatnam
e: Detailed Explanation: The common law system based on recorded judicial precedents began in India with the establishment of Mayor's Courts in the three major presidency towns of Madras, Bombay, and Calcutta by the East India Company in 1726.

qe: Under the judicial framework designed by Warren Hastings in 1772, the newly established District Diwani Adalats were placed under the direct administrative charge of which official?
qh: 1772 में वॉरेन हेस्टिंग्स द्वारा तैयार किए गए न्यायिक ढांचे के तहत, नव स्थापित जिला दीवानी अदालतों को किस अधिकारी के सीधे प्रशासनिक प्रभार में रखा गया था?
o: The Collector
The Chief Qazi
The District Judge
The Commissioner of Revenue
e: Detailed Explanation: Warren Hastings established District Diwani Adalats to try civil disputes. These courts were placed directly under the administrative charge of the district Collector, and they applied Hindu law for Hindus and Muslim law for Muslims.

qe: During the judicial administration of Warren Hastings, the highest court of criminal appeal that reviewed capital punishment and required the signature of a Deputy Nizam was the:
qh: वॉरेन हेस्टिंग्स के न्यायिक प्रशासन के दौरान, आपराधिक अपील की सर्वोच्च अदालत कौन सी थी जो मृत्युदंड की समीक्षा करती थी और जिसके लिए डिप्टी निजाम के हस्ताक्षर की आवश्यकता होती थी?
o: Sadar Nizamat Adalat
Sadar Diwani Adalat
District Fauzdari Adalat
Supreme Court of Calcutta
e: Detailed Explanation: The District Fauzdari Adalats tried criminal cases locally, but the final approval for capital punishment (death penalty) and forfeiture of property rested with the Sadar Nizamat Adalat, which initially operated at Murshidabad under a Deputy Nizam.

qe: The Regulating Act of 1773 led to the historic creation of a Supreme Court at Calcutta. What structural limitation frequently disrupted its operational efficiency in its early years?
qh: 1773 के रेगुलेटिंग एक्ट के कारण कलकत्ता में एक सर्वोच्च न्यायालय की ऐतिहासिक स्थापना हुई। इसके शुरुआती वर्षों में किस संरचनात्मक सीमा ने इसकी परिचालन दक्षता को बार-बार बाधित किया?
o: Its jurisdiction frequently clashed with that of the Company's mofussil adalats
It was completely barred from trying British subjects
It lacked original jurisdiction over criminal disputes
It was legally subordinate to the Sadar Diwani Adalat
e: Detailed Explanation: The Supreme Court established at Calcutta under the Regulating Act of 1773 was competent to try all British subjects. However, the Act did not clearly demarcate its relations with the Company's courts, causing frequent jurisdictional clashes between the Supreme Court and the Sadar/mofussil adalats.

qe: The judicial code introduced by Lord Cornwallis between 1786 and 1793 was structurally anchored on which major administrative principle?
qh: 1786 और 1793 के बीच लॉर्ड कॉर्नवॉलिस द्वारा पेश की गई न्यायिक संहिता संरचनात्मक रूप से किस प्रमुख प्रशासनिक सिद्धांत पर आधारित थी?
o: Separation of Powers
The absolute centralization of financial collections
The revival of traditional village panchayat structures
Exemption of government officials from civil jurisdiction
e: Detailed Explanation: The Cornwallis Code of 1793 was explicitly based on the principle of the Separation of Powers. It separated revenue administration from judicial administration, divesting the Collector of magisterial and judicial duties.

qe: Lord Cornwallis systematically abolished the District Fauzdari Courts. To replace them as intermediate courts of appeal for both civil and criminal disputes, he established Circuit Courts at which four locations?
qh: लॉर्ड कॉर्नवॉलिस ने जिला फौजदारी अदालतों को व्यवस्थित रूप से समाप्त कर दिया। दीवानी और आपराधिक दोनों विवादों के लिए अपील की मध्यवर्ती अदालतों के रूप में उनके स्थान पर उन्होंने किन चार स्थानों पर सर्किट कोर्ट (Circuit Courts) स्थापित किए?
o: Calcutta, Dacca, Murshidabad, and Patna
Calcutta, Bombay, Madras, and Allahabad
Patna, Gaya, Shahabad, and Bhagalpur
Surat, Masulipatnam, Madras, and Cochin
e: Detailed Explanation: Cornwallis replaced the District Fauzdari Courts with four provincial Circuit Courts established at Calcutta, Dacca, Murshidabad, and Patna. These courts were presided over by European judges and acted as courts of appeal.

qe: Following the separation of revenue and justice under the Cornwallis Code, the District Diwani Adalat was designated as the Zila Court and placed under the charge of which explicit official?
qh: कॉर्नवॉलिस कोड के तहत राजस्व और न्याय के अलगाव के बाद, जिला दीवानी अदालत को जिला या जिला न्यायालय (Zila Court) के रूप में नामित किया गया और किस अधिकारी के प्रभार में रखा गया?
o: A specialized District Judge
The Revenue Collector
The Chief Mufti
The Provincial Commissioner
e: Detailed Explanation: Under the Cornwallis Code, the District Diwani Adalat was placed under a newly designated District Judge. The Collector's functions were strictly limited to revenue administration, stripping them of all magisterial duties.

qe: Under the structural hierarchy of civil courts established by Cornwallis, which court stood at the lowest tier, managed directly by Indian officers?
qh: कॉर्नवॉलिस द्वारा स्थापित दीवानी अदालतों के पदानुक्रम में, कौन सी अदालत सबसे निचले स्तर पर थी, जिसका प्रबंधन सीधे भारतीय अधिकारियों द्वारा किया जाता था?
o: Munsiff's Court
Registrar's Court
Zila Court
Circuit Court
e: Detailed Explanation: Cornwallis organized a regular gradation of civil courts. The lowest tier was the Munsiff's Court, which was placed under Indian officers, followed upward by the Registrar's Court (under a European judge), the District/Zila Court, the Circuit Courts, and the Sadar Diwani Adalat.

qe: The judicial framework of the Cornwallis Code established a major constitutional milestone in colonial India by introducing which principle?
qh: कॉर्नवॉलिस कोड के न्यायिक ढांचे ने किस सिद्धांत की शुरुआत करके औपनिवेशिक भारत में एक प्रमुख संवैधानिक मील का पत्थर स्थापित किया?
o: Sovereignty of law and accountability of government officials to civil courts
Absolute legal immunity for European subjects in criminal acts
The mandatory use of vernacular languages across all appellate benches
The complete financial independence of the provincial governments
e: Detailed Explanation: The Cornwallis Code established the sovereignty of law. It declared that government officials were answerable to civil courts for actions done in their official capacity, bringing administration under legal oversight.

qe: During the administrative updates introduced by Lord William Bentinck (1828–1833), the provincial Circuit Courts were abolished. Their judicial and operational functions were transferred to:
qh: लॉर्ड विलियम बेंटिक (1828-1833) द्वारा शुरू किए गए प्रशासनिक सुधारों के दौरान, प्रांतीय सर्किट कोर्ट को समाप्त कर दिया गया था। उनके न्यायिक और परिचालन कार्य किसे हस्तांतरित किए गए थे?
o: Collectors under the supervision of the Commissioner of Revenue and Circuit
Munsiffs operating inside local lower subdivisions
The King-in-Council based in London directly
The Registrar's benches attached to Zila Courts
e: Detailed Explanation: Lord William Bentinck abolished the four provincial Circuit Courts because they caused delays in justice. Their functions were transferred to district Collectors, who were placed under the strict supervision of the newly created Commissioners of Revenue and Circuit.

qe: To provide convenient judicial access to the population of the Upper Provinces, Lord William Bentinck established a separate Sadar Diwani Adalat and a Sadar Nizamat Adalat at which location?
qh: उच्च प्रांतों (Upper Provinces) की आबादी को सुविधाजनक न्यायिक पहुंच प्रदान करने के लिए, लॉर्ड विलियम बेंटिक ने किस स्थान पर एक अलग सदर दीवानी अदालत और एक सदर निजामत अदालत की स्थापना की?
o: Allahabad
Patna
Calcutta
Murshidabad
e: Detailed Explanation: For the convenience of the people of the Upper Provinces (who previously had to travel all the way to Calcutta), Lord William Bentinck set up a separate Sadar Diwani Adalat and a Sadar Nizamat Adalat at Allahabad.

qe: Before Lord William Bentinck's language reforms, Persian was the sole official language of the colonial courts. What major linguistic change did Bentinck introduce?
qh: लॉर्ड विलियम बेंटिक के भाषा सुधारों से पहले, फारसी औपनिवेशिक अदालतों की एकमात्र आधिकारिक भाषा थी। बेंटिक ने कौन सा बड़ा भाषाई बदलाव पेश किया?
o: He gave suitors the option to use Persian or their local vernacular language in lower courts, while English replaced Persian in the Supreme Court
He made Sanskrit mandatory for all civil disputes involving Hindu subjects
He completely banned the use of English across all levels of appellate jurisdiction
He enforced Arabic as the sole language for criminal courts
e: Detailed Explanation: Bentinck introduced a major language reform by allowing suitors the option to use either Persian or their local vernacular language in lower courts. In the Supreme Court, English completely replaced Persian as the official language.

qe: In 1833, a Law Commission was set up under the chairmanship of Lord Macaulay. This commission laid the foundation for preparing which core legal codes of India?
qh: 1833 में, लॉर्ड मैकाले की अध्यक्षता में एक विधि आयोग (Law Commission) का गठन किया गया था। इस आयोग ने भारत के किन मुख्य कानूनी संहिताओं को तैयार करने की नींव रखी?
o: The Civil Procedure Code (1859), the Indian Penal Code (1860), and the Criminal Procedure Code (1861)
The Cornwallis Code updates and the Regulating guidelines of 1773
The Federal Court Jurisdiction acts and the High Court merger charters
The Local Self-Government taxation schedules and municipal codes
e: Detailed Explanation: The first Law Commission under Macaulay was appointed under the Charter Act of 1833. Its codification work resulted in the drafting of the Civil Procedure Code (1859), the Indian Penal Code (1860), and the Criminal Procedure Code (1861).

qe: The Indian High Courts Act of 1861 led to a massive structural consolidation of the higher judiciary in 1865. This consolidation was achieved by:
qh: 1861 के भारतीय उच्च न्यायालय अधिनियम के कारण 1865 में उच्च न्यायपालिका का एक बड़ा संरचनात्मक सुदृढ़ीकरण हुआ। यह सुदृढ़ीकरण कैसे प्राप्त किया गया था?
o: Merging the Supreme Court and the Sadar Adalats into three High Courts at Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras
Abolishing all Zila courts in favor of centralized provincial circuit benches
Subordinating the High Courts directly to the newly established Federal Court of India
Transferring all appellate magisterial functions back to the district collectors
e: Detailed Explanation: In 1865, the dual system of the higher judiciary was eliminated by merging the Crown's Supreme Courts and the Company's Sadar Diwani and Sadar Nizamat Adalats into three unified High Courts at Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras.

qe: The Government of India Act of 1935 provided for the creation of a Federal Court, which was formally set up in 1937. What was its primary jurisdiction?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1935 ने एक संघीय न्यायालय (Federal Court) के निर्माण का प्रावधान किया, जिसे औपचारिक रूप से 1937 में स्थापित किया गया था। इसका प्राथमिक अधिकार क्षेत्र क्या था?
o: To settle disputes between different governments and hear limited appeals from the High Courts
To directly try European subjects involved in severe criminal acts inside rural provinces
To oversee the tax revenue collections of local municipal district boards
To act as the final absolute court of appeal above the British King-in-Council
e: Detailed Explanation: The Federal Court, set up in 1937 under the 1935 Act, had the jurisdiction to solve disputes between provinces and the center (or between provinces) and to hear limited constitutional appeals from the High Courts. It was the precursor to the Supreme Court of India.

qe: Despite establishing the 'Rule of Law', what structural drawback heavily criticized the British judicial system in India from the perspective of ordinary citizens?
qh: 'कानून का शासन' स्थापित करने के बावजूद, आम नागरिकों के दृष्टिकोण से भारत में ब्रिटिश न्यायिक प्रणाली की किस संरचनात्मक कमी की भारी आलोचना की गई थी?
o: The system became highly complicated, slow, and expensive, allowing the rich to manipulate it
It completely lacked any written or codified legal regulations
It refused to allow European subjects to be brought under civil court oversight
It completely subordinated judicial benches to the traditional village zamindars
e: Detailed Explanation: A major negative aspect of the British judicial system was its highly complicated, technical, and expensive nature. Litigation dragged out for years, creating an environment where the wealthy could manipulate the system through deceit and false evidence.

qe: Following the cataclysmic events of the 1857 Revolt, what major shift occurred in the global economic landscape that triggered a 'new stage of colonialism' in India?
qh: 1857 के विद्रोह की विनाशकारी घटनाओं के बाद, वैश्विक आर्थिक परिदृश्य में कौन सा बड़ा बदलाव आया जिसने भारत में 'औपनिवेशिक शासन के एक नए चरण' को जन्म दिया?
o: The intensification of the Industrial Revolution and the emergence of new industrial powers like the USA, Japan, and European nations creating cut-throat competition for markets
The complete collapse of the global maritime shipping and trade lines across Europe
The absolute abandonment of British capital investments inside the Indian railway networks
The total financial bankruptcy of the British Parliament and its Crown tracking systems
e: Detailed Explanation: In the second half of the 19th century, the rapid industrialization of the USA, Japan, and continental Europe broke Britain's industrial monopoly. This cut-throat international competition for raw materials and captive markets forced Britain to tighten its imperial control over India to secure its commercial and financial interests.

qe: The landmark 'Act for Better Government of India, 1858' introduced a profound constitutional shift in the administration of India by:
qh: ऐतिहासिक 'Act for Better Government of India, 1858' ने भारत के प्रशासन में कौन सा गहरा संवैधानिक बदलाव पेश किया?
o: Transferring the power to govern from the East India Company directly to the British Crown
Establishing complete provincial autonomy under popular native ministerial portfolios
Abolishing the office of the Viceroy and creating the separate Federal Court structure
Scrapping the supervisory control of the British Parliament over Indian revenues
e: Detailed Explanation: The Government of India Act of 1858 dissolved the East India Company following the 1857 Revolt. It transferred the sovereign power to govern India directly to the British Crown, ending the Company's rule.

qe: Under the administrative framework introduced after 1858, the dual system of control established by Pitt's India Act of 1784 was abolished. The power to govern was concentrated in which office based in London?
qh: 1858 के बाद शुरू किए गए प्रशासनिक ढांचे के तहत, 1784 के पिट्स इंडिया एक्ट द्वारा स्थापित नियंत्रण की दोहरी प्रणाली को समाप्त कर दिया गया था। शासन करने की शक्ति लंदन में स्थित किस कार्यालय में केंद्रित थी?
o: The Secretary of State for India assisted by a council of 15
The Board of Directors of the renewed corporate charter
The Executive Council of the Supreme Governor-General
The High Commissioner for South Asian Colonial Affairs
e: Detailed Explanation: The Act of 1858 replaced the Company's Directors and the Board of Control with the Secretary of State for India. The Secretary of State was a member of the British Cabinet, answerable to Parliament, and was assisted by an advisory council of 15 members.

qe: The structural administrative changes introduced by the Indian Councils Act of 1861 expanded the Viceroy's executive council for legislative purposes. What was a major institutional weakness of this Legislative Council?
qh: भारतीय परिषद अधिनियम 1861 द्वारा शुरू किए गए संरचनात्मक प्रशासनिक परिवर्तनों ने विधायी उद्देश्यों के लिए वायसराय की कार्यकारी परिषद का विस्तार किया। इस विधान परिषद (Legislative Council) की एक प्रमुख संस्थागत कमजोरी क्या थी?
o: It was entirely advisory in nature, possessed no real power over executive action, and could not discuss financial budgets
It held absolute sovereign veto power over the decisions of the British Cabinet
It was composed entirely of lower-caste revolutionary peasant leaders from rural provinces
It could independently pass international maritime trade laws without the Viceroy's approval
e: Detailed Explanation: The Legislative Council created by the Act of 1861 was merely advisory. It had no control over the budget, could not discuss executive actions or crucial financial matters without previous government approval, and its bills could be vetoed by the Viceroy or disallowed by the Secretary of State.

qe: The Indian Councils Act of 1861 modified the provincial administrative architecture by restoring legislative powers to which specific provinces, reversing a centralization trend begun in 1833?
qh: भारतीय परिषद अधिनियम 1861 ने किन विशिष्ट प्रांतों को विधायी शक्तियां बहाल करके प्रांतीय प्रशासनिक संरचना को संशोधित किया, जिससे 1833 में शुरू हुई केंद्रीकरण की प्रवृत्ति उलट गई?
o: Madras and Bombay
Bengal and the North-Western Province
Punjab and Assam
Bihar and Orissa
e: Detailed Explanation: The Charter Act of 1833 had centralized legislation by stripping the provinces of their legislative powers. The Indian Councils Act of 1861 reversed this trend by returning legislative authority to the presidencies of Madras and Bombay.

qe: In the structural history of colonial public finance, who initiated the very first formal step towards financial decentralization in 1870 by bifurcating central and provincial finances for specific local services?
qh: औपनिवेशिक सार्वजनिक वित्त के संरचनात्मक इतिहास में, किसने 1870 में विशिष्ट स्थानीय सेवाओं के लिए केंद्रीय और प्रांतीय वित्त को विभाजित करके वित्तीय विकेंद्रीकरण (financial decentralization) की दिशा में पहला औपचारिक कदम शुरू किया था?
o: Lord Mayo
Lord Lytton
Lord Ripon
Lord Curzon
e: Detailed Explanation: Lord Mayo took the first step toward financial decentralization in 1870 by granting fixed sums out of central revenues to provincial governments to manage local services like police, jails, education, medical facilities, and roads.

qe: In 1882, a system divided all sources of colonial revenue into three structural groups: general (entirely central), provincial (entirely provincial), and divided heads. Under whose administration was this enacted?
qh: 1882 में, एक प्रणाली ने औपनिवेशिक राजस्व के सभी स्रोतों को तीन संरचनात्मक समूहों में विभाजित किया: सामान्य (पूरी तरह से केंद्रीय), प्रांतीय (पूरी तरह से प्रांतीय), और विभाजित प्रमुख। यह किसके प्रशासन के तहत अधिनियमित किया गया था?
o: Lord Ripon
Lord Mayo
Lord Lytton
Lord Elgin
e: Detailed Explanation: Following Mayo's 1870 steps and Lytton's 1877 extensions, Lord Ripon's administration in 1882 systematic divided revenue sources into three distinct groups: central, provincial, and divided heads (shared between center and provinces).

qe: Between 1864 and 1868, early local bodies were formed across various districts in British India. What was their primary practical function from the perspective of the local population?
qh: 1864 और 1868 के बीच, ब्रिटिश भारत में विभिन्न जिलों में शुरुआती स्थानीय निकायों का गठन किया गया था। स्थानीय आबादी के दृष्टिकोण से उनका प्राथमिक व्यावहारिक कार्य क्या था?
o: They operated merely as instruments of additional tax collection headed by district magistrates
They provided full sovereign democratic representation to landless peasants
They functioned as independent legal aid clinics managing high court appeals
They were designed to actively eliminate the revenue collection powers of the center
e: Detailed Explanation: The early local bodies formed between 1864 and 1868 lacked democratic elements. They consisted mostly of nominated members, were headed by the District Magistrate, and were used by the administration primarily as instruments to collect additional local taxes.

qe: Lord Mayo's Resolution of 1870 on financial decentralization directly authorized provincial governments to implement which measure to balance their local budgets?
qh: वित्तीय विकेंद्रीकरण पर लॉर्ड मेयो के 1870 के प्रस्ताव ने प्रांतीय सरकारों को अपने स्थानीय बजट को संतुलित करने के लिए कौन सा उपाय लागू करने के लिए सीधे अधिकृत किया था?
o: To resort to localized taxation to manage services like sanitation and roads
To completely print independent regional fiat currencies without central tracking
To seize all private property assets held by urban banking captains
To refuse any onward transmission of land revenue shares to London
e: Detailed Explanation: Mayo's Resolution of 1870 linked financial decentralization with local governance. Along with a fixed central grant, it authorized provinces to levy local taxes to balance budgets for managing public works, sanitation, and education.

qe: Who is universally celebrated in modern Indian history as the 'Father of Local Self-Government in India' due to his landmark Resolution of 1882?
qh: आधुनिक भारतीय इतिहास में किसे उनके 1882 के ऐतिहासिक प्रस्ताव के कारण 'भारत में स्थानीय स्वशासन के जनक' (Father of Local Self-Government in India) के रूप में सार्वभौमिक रूप से सराहा जाता है?
o: Lord Ripon
Lord Mayo
Lord Lytton
Lord William Bentinck
e: Detailed Explanation: Lord Ripon is called the father of local self-government in India. His landmark Resolution of 1882 laid down guidelines for establishing urban and rural local bodies with non-official majorities and elected members to foster political education.

qe: Lord Ripon's Resolution of 1882 on local self-government outlined specific democratic structural principles. Which of the following was a key feature of this resolution?
qh: स्थानीय स्वशासन पर लॉर्ड रिपन के 1882 के प्रस्ताव में विशिष्ट लोकतांत्रिक संरचनात्मक सिद्धांतों की रूपरेखा तैयार की गई थी। इस प्रस्ताव की मुख्य विशेषता निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी थी?
o: Non-officials to be in the majority and to act as chairpersons of these local bodies
Official district magistrates to permanently dictate all inner tax policies manually
The complete removal of any legal requirement for official executive executive sanctions
Restricting vote franchise exclusively to landless lower-caste agricultural ryots
e: Detailed Explanation: Ripon's Resolution recommended that local bodies should feature a majority of non-officials, who should ideally be elected, and that these non-officials should act as chairpersons of the boards, minimizing direct official interference.

qe: Despite the liberal vision of Lord Ripon's 1882 Resolution, the practical implementation of local self-government faced severe drawbacks. Which of the following reflects a major limitation of these existing bodies?
qh: लॉर्ड रिपन के 1882 के प्रस्ताव के उदारवादी दृष्टिकोण के बावजूद, स्थानीय स्वशासन के व्यावहारिक कार्यान्वयन को गंभीर कमियों का सामना करना पड़ा। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा इन निकायों की एक बड़ी सीमा को दर्शाता है?
o: The franchise was highly limited, and the government retained strict powers to suspend or supersede these bodies at will
The elected members held an absolute sovereign majority across all rural district boards
The district officials were completely legally barred from inspecting financial accounts
Local bodies possessed unrestricted powers to enhance terminal taxes on all trades
e: Explanation: In practice, the bureaucracy undermined Ripon's reforms. The franchise remained highly restricted, elected members were a minority on many boards, district officials continued to dominate, and the provincial governments retained the power to suspend or supersede these local bodies at will.

qe: During the opening decade of the 20th century, which high priest of imperialism took active regressive steps to drastically increase official state control over local self-governing bodies?
qh: 20वीं शताब्दी के पहले दशक के दौरान, साम्राज्यवाद के किस प्रबल समर्थक ने स्थानीय स्वशासी निकायों पर आधिकारिक राज्य नियंत्रण को काफी बढ़ाने के लिए प्रतिगामी कदम उठाए थे?
o: Lord Curzon
Lord Lytton
Lord Dufferin
Lord Lansdowne
e: Detailed Explanation: The closing decades of the 19th century and early 20th century saw an upsurge in imperialist policy. Lord Curzon, an ardent centralizer, enacted measures to systematically curb the autonomy of local bodies and increase official bureaucratic control over them.

qe: The Royal Commission on Decentralization was appointed in 1908 to look into structural obstacles facing local governance. What did it identify as the great 'stumbling block' to their effective functioning?
qh: स्थानीय शासन के सामने आने वाली संरचनात्मक बाधाओं की जांच के लिए 1908 में रॉयल कमीशन ऑन विकेंद्रीकरण (Royal Commission on Decentralization) नियुक्त किया गया था। इसने उनके प्रभावी कामकाज में सबसे बड़ी 'बाधा' (stumbling block) के रूप में किसे पहचाना?
o: The acute lack of adequate financial resources and independent taxation powers
The complete legal absorption of all local bodies by the Indian National Congress
The heavy presence of highly educated lower-caste non-officials on the benches
The manual interference of the British King-in-Council in petty village judicial cases
e: Detailed Explanation: The Royal Commission on Decentralization (1908) pointed out that the lack of financial resources was the great stumbling block in the effective functioning of local self-governing bodies, and recommended widening their taxation powers.

qe: Which of the following structural recommendations was explicitly made by the Royal Commission on Decentralization (1908) to revitalize rural local governance?
qh: ग्रामीण स्थानीय शासन को पुनर्जीवित करने के लिए रॉयल कमीशन ऑन विकेंद्रीकरण (1908) द्वारा निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा संरचनात्मक सुझाव विशेष रूप से दिया गया था?
o: Village panchayats should be entrusted with more powers, including judicial jurisdiction in petty cases and separate sources of income
The complete and immediate administrative abolition of all sub-district taluka boards
Making grants-in-aid from provincial governments mandatory and regular for all minor maintenance works
Subordinating the entire municipal infrastructure directly to the central executive councillor
e: Detailed Explanation: To strengthen rural administration, the 1908 Commission recommended that village panchayats be revived and entrusted with more powers—such as handling petty judicial cases, maintaining village schools, and managing local public works—along with separate sources of income.

qe: Under the constitutional framework of the Government of India Act 1919, local self-government was made a 'transferred' subject. Why were Indian popular ministers still unable to execute significant work in this sphere?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1919 के संवैधानिक ढांचे के तहत, स्थानीय स्वशासन को एक 'हस्तांतरित' (transferred) विषय बनाया गया था। इसके बावजूद भारतीय लोकप्रिय मंत्री इस क्षेत्र में महत्वपूर्ण कार्य करने में असमर्थ क्यों रहे?
o: Because Finance remained a 'reserved' subject under the charge of an executive councillor, leaving them with a severe lack of funds
Because the local municipal boards completely refused to accept popular native leaders
Because the Act explicitly barred ministers from passing any provincial legislative codes
Because the tracking loops of local taxation were entirely Scrapped by the British Crown
e: Detailed Explanation: Under Dyarchy (introduced by the 1919 Act), local government was a 'transferred' subject under Indian ministers. However, because the crucial portfolio of Finance was kept as a 'reserved' subject under a British Executive Councillor, Indian ministers faced a severe lack of funds, crippling their development initiatives.

qe: The Simon Commission, in its May 1930 report, reviewed local self-governing bodies. What retrograde step did it suggest regarding their efficiency parameters?
qh: साइमन कमीशन ने मई 1930 की अपनी रिपोर्ट में स्थानीय स्वशासी निकायों की समीक्षा की थी। इसने उनकी दक्षता के मापदंडों के संबंध में कौन सा प्रतिगामी कदम (retrograde step) सुझाया था?
o: Increasing provincial bureaucratic control over local bodies for the sake of efficiency
The complete tracking and legal dissolution of all active village panchayats in Madras
The immediate transfer of the entire finance portfolio to popular native ministries
Scrapping any requirement for local franchise qualifications across the board
e: Detailed Explanation: The Simon Commission report (1930) noted a deterioration in the financial management of local bodies since 1919. Instead of recommending democratic expansion, it suggested a retrograde step: increasing provincial government control over local bodies in the name of administrative efficiency.

qe: How did the advent of 'Provincial Autonomy' under the Government of India Act 1935 positively impact the development of local self-governing institutions in India?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1935 के तहत 'प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता' (Provincial Autonomy) के आगमन ने भारत में स्थानीय स्वशासी संस्थानों के विकास को सकारात्मक रूप से कैसे प्रभावित किया?
o: Portfolio finance came under the control of popular ministries, making funds available for the development of local bodies
It completely abolished the legal collection of all local and municipal professional taxes
It forced provincial governors to manually head every city municipality board bench
It legally transferred the ultimate supervisory control over local works directly to the Federal Court
e: Detailed Explanation: The introduction of Provincial Autonomy under the 1935 Act placed the entire provincial administration, including the Finance portfolio, under elected popular ministries. This allowed popular governments to allocate adequate funds and pass progressive legislative Acts to expand the powers of local bodies.

qe: Despite structural changes after the 1935 Act, what regressive financial restriction was placed by the center on the taxation powers of local municipal bodies?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के बाद संरचनात्मक परिवर्तनों के बावजूद, स्थानीय नगरपालिका निकायों की कराधान शक्तियों पर केंद्र द्वारा कौन सा प्रतिगामी वित्तीय प्रतिबंध लगाया गया था?
o: Restrictions were placed on their powers to levy or enhance terminal taxes on trades, callings, professions, and municipal property
They were completely barred from accepting any form of voluntary local charity contributions
They were legally forced to route 100% of their collected local taxes directly to the British Treasury in London
They were prohibited from running any primary or middle vernacular schools inside their boundaries
e: Detailed Explanation: After 1935, despite overall political advance, the colonial center placed new restrictions that capped or limited the powers of local municipal bodies to levy or enhance terminal taxes on trades, callings, professions, and municipal properties, ignoring the decentralization recommendations of 1908.

qe: Which Article of the Constitution of free India directs the state governments to organize village panchayats as effective organs of local self-government?
qh: स्वतंत्र भारत के संविधान का कौन सा अनुच्छेद राज्य सरकारों को ग्राम पंचायतों को स्थानीय स्वशासन के प्रभावी अंगों के रूप में संगठित करने का निर्देश देता है?
o: Article 40
Article 32
Article 200
Article 312
e: Detailed Explanation: Article 40, contained within the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV) of the Indian Constitution, explicitly directs the State to take active steps to organize village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of local self-government.

qe: Which specific constitutional amendments were enacted in free India to plug structural loopholes and provide constitutional status to local self-governing institutions in rural and urban areas respectively?
qh: स्वतंत्र भारत में संरचनात्मक कमियों को दूर करने और क्रमशः ग्रामीण और शहरी क्षेत्रों में स्थानीय स्वशासी संस्थानों को संवैधानिक दर्जा देने के लिए कौन से विशिष्ट संवैधानिक संशोधन अधिनियमित किए गए थे?
o: 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Amendments
42nd and 44th Constitutional Amendment Amendments
24th and 25th Constitutional Amendment Amendments
86th and 91st Constitutional Amendment Amendments
e: Detailed Explanation: The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts passed in 1992 institutionalized local self-government in India by providing a constitutional framework for Panchayati Raj Institutions (rural) and Municipalities (urban) respectively.

qe: A certain project requires a structural mapping coordinate grid setup. If a vehicle moves dynamically 24 km North from point A, and then drives 7 km East to reach target point B, find the absolute straight-line distance from A to B.
qh: एक वाहन बिंदु A से 24 किमी उत्तर की ओर चलता है, और फिर पूर्व की ओर 7 किमी गाड़ी चलाकर बिंदु B पर पहुँचता है। A से B की सीधी रेखा की दूरी ज्ञात कीजिए।
o: 25 km
31 km
28 km
30 km
e:
Detailed Explanation: This spatial movement forms a right-angled triangle with base legs of 24 km and 7 km. The straight-line distance is the hypotenuse.
By Pythagoras theorem: $\text{Distance} = \sqrt{24^2 + 7^2} = \sqrt{576 + 49} = \sqrt{625} = \mathbf{25\text{ km}}$.

qe: In an ecosystem dynamic survey, if the Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) is measured at 35,000 units and the respiratory losses (R) of the primary producers accumulate to 15,000 units, calculate the Net Primary Productivity (NPP).
qh: एक पारितंत्र गतिशीलता सर्वेक्षण में, यदि सकल प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (GPP) 35,000 इकाइयाँ मापी जाती है और प्राथमिक उत्पादकों की श्वसन हानि (R) 15,000 इकाइयाँ संचित होती है, तो शुद्ध प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (NPP) की गणना करें।
o: 20,000 units
50,000 units
15,000 units
30,000 units
e:
Detailed Explanation: Applying the fundamental ecological productivity equation: $NPP = GPP - R$.
Substituting the given value fields: $NPP = 35,000 - 15,000 = \mathbf{20,000\text{ units}}$.

qe: The 'Cornwallis Code' of 1793 brought a radical structural change in the colonial judicial administration by introducing which concept regarding European subjects?
qh: 1793 के 'कॉर्नवॉलिस कोड' ने यूरोपीय विषयों (European subjects) के संबंध में किस अवधारणा को पेश करके औपनिवेशिक न्यायिक प्रशासन में एक क्रांतिकारी संरचनात्मक बदलाव लाया?
o: It brought European subjects completely under the jurisdiction of the civil courts
It granted European subjects complete absolute immunity from all civil and criminal judicial trials
It mandated that European subjects could only be tried inside the lower Munsiff's courts managed by Indian officers
It completely barred European subjects from purchasing private property in land within the Bengal Presidency
e: Detailed Explanation: A major feature of the Cornwallis Code was that it brought European subjects under the jurisdiction of the civil courts for civil matters, ending their relative legal isolation from local administrative courts.

qe: Under the financial decentralization scheme introduced by Lord Lytton in 1877, which specific provincial revenue tracking heads were transferred directly to the control of provincial governments?
qh: 1877 में लॉर्ड लिटन द्वारा शुरू की गई वित्तीय विकेंद्रीकरण योजना के तहत, कौन से विशिष्ट प्रांतीय राजस्व ट्रैकिंग प्रमुख सीधे प्रांतीय सरकारों के नियंत्रण में स्थानांतरित किए गए थे?
o: Land revenue, excise, general administration, and law and justice
Customs duties, salt monopolies, and central maritime commissions exclusively
The printing of regional military bills and currency tracking parameters
The absolute control over international trade networks plying along the coasts
e: Detailed Explanation: In 1877, Lord Lytton expanded financial decentralization by transferring heads of expenditure like land revenue, excise, general administration, and law and justice to the provinces, along with a fixed share of provincial income derived from stamps and local income taxes.

qe: What structural limitation regarding the selection of non-official Indian members in the Legislative Council under the Act of 1861 failed to represent true public opinion?
qh: अधिनियम 1861 के तहत विधान परिषद में गैर-आधिकारिक भारतीय सदस्यों के चयन के संबंध में कौन सी संरचनात्मक सीमा वास्तविक जनमत का प्रतिनिधित्व करने में विफल रही?
o: The associated non-official Indians were drawn exclusively from elite sections like princes, big landlords, and diwans
The members were chosen via an open democratic universal adult franchise tracking system
The positions were restricted strictly to landless lower-caste agricultural ryots from backward subdivisions
The Indian members were required to hold highly technical engineering degrees from British universities
e: Detailed Explanation: The non-official Indian members associated with the Legislative Council under the Indian Councils Act of 1861 were not representatives of the common public; they were handpicked by the Viceroy exclusively from elite loyalist sections—such as ruling princes, wealthy landlords, and retired diwans.

qe: The judicial reforms introduced by Lord Cornwallis completely shifted the functional profile of the district Collector. What was the Collector's primary responsibility after 1793?
qh: लॉर्ड कॉर्नवॉलिस द्वारा शुरू किए गए न्यायिक सुधारों ने जिला कलेक्टर के कार्यात्मक प्रोफ़ाइल को पूरी तरह से बदल दिया। 1793 के बाद कलेक्टर की प्राथमिक जिम्मेदारी क्या थी?
o: He was responsible solely for revenue administration with no magisterial or judicial functions
He held supreme absolute veto power over all regional criminal circuit court decisions
He was transformed into the chief executive judge of the Sadar Nizamat Adalat at Calcutta
He directly oversaw the recruitment and competitive examinations of the native civil services
e: Detailed Explanation: Under the Cornwallis Code, the Collector was divested of all judicial and magisterial powers. His responsibility was confined strictly to revenue administration, bringing an end to the concentration of fiscal and judicial authority in a single office.

qe: The 'Mayo’s Resolution of 1870' is highly significant in the history of local governance in India because it marked the formal beginning of:
qh: लॉर्ड मेयो का 1870 का प्रस्ताव भारत में स्थानीय शासन के इतिहास में अत्यधिक महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि इसने किसकी औपचारिक शुरुआत को चिह्नित किया था?
o: Local finance through municipal acts allowing local taxation to balance budgets
The total administrative bifurcation of the Supreme Court and High Court benches
An absolute mass universal adult franchise system across all rural district boards
The permanent legal abolition of the office of the Secretary of State for India
e: Detailed Explanation: Mayo's Resolution of 1870 marked the real beginning of local finance in India. It authorized provincial governments to enact municipal acts and resort to local taxation to balance budgets for managing public health, roads, and education.

qe: Under the judicial gradation established by the Cornwallis Code, where did the final absolute right of appeal lie for high-value civil suits involving 5,000 pounds and above?
qh: कॉर्नवॉलिस कोड द्वारा स्थापित न्यायिक पदानुक्रम के तहत, 5,000 पाउंड और उससे अधिक के उच्च मूल्य वाले दीवानी मुकदमों के लिए अपील का अंतिम पूर्ण अधिकार कहाँ था?
o: The King-in-Council based in London
The Sadar Diwani Adalat at Calcutta
The Provincial Circuit Court of Appeal
The High Court of Judicature Bench
e: Detailed Explanation: In the civil court hierarchy established by Cornwallis, appeals from the Zila Courts went to the provincial Circuit Courts, then to the Sadar Diwani Adalat at Calcutta. For extraordinarily high-value disputes involving 5,000 pounds and above, the final right of appeal lay with the King-in-Council in London.

qe: The Government of India Act of 1858 created a 15-member council to assist the Secretary of State for India. What was the functional nature of this Council?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1858 ने भारत के राज्य सचिव की सहायता के लिए एक 15 सदस्यीय परिषद का गठन किया। इस परिषद की कार्यात्मक प्रकृति क्या थी?
o: It was purely advisory in nature, and final initiatives and decisions rested entirely with the Secretary of State
It possessed absolute sovereign legislative veto power over the British Parliament
It was composed entirely of elected non-official popular Indian ministers from provincial legislatures
It held direct operational command over the judicial administration of the Federal Court
e: Detailed Explanation: The 15-member Council of India established under the 1858 Act was strictly advisory. The ultimate decision-making power and initiative rested with the Secretary of State, who could override the council's recommendations.

qe: Why did the administrative changes introduced after the 1857 Revolt prioritize the association of wealthy native elites, like princes and landlords, into the legislative advisory bodies?
qh: 1857 के विद्रोह के बाद शुरू किए गए प्रशासनिक परिवर्तनों ने अमीर मूल अभिजात वर्ग (जैसे राजकुमारों और जमींदारों) को विधायी सलाहकार निकायों में शामिल करने को प्राथमिकता क्यों दी?
o: To narrow the ruler-subject gap and gain a better tracking idea of local customs and values to handle future crises tactfully
To completely transfer the control of portfolio finance directly to popular lower-caste ministries
To systematically prepare a cadre of selfless national missionaries for total secular public education
To launch an aggressive legislative campaign designed to abolish the rigid hereditary chaturvarna system
e: Detailed Explanation: The British learned from 1857 that mass alienation could threaten their rule. By associating native elites into advisory bodies, they aimed to create a conservative political buffer, bridge the absolute ruler-subject gap, and monitor local public opinion to prevent future rebellions.

qe: In the administrative reorganization after 1858, what operational title was newly added to the office of the Governor-General of India to reflect his role as the direct representative of the British Crown?
qh: 1858 के बाद प्रशासनिक पुनर्गठन में, भारत के गवर्नर-जनरल के कार्यालय में ब्रिटिश क्राउन के सीधे प्रतिनिधि के रूप में उनकी भूमिका को दर्शाने के लिए कौन सा नया परिचालन शीर्षक जोड़ा गया था?
o: Viceroy
Secretary of State
Chief Commissioner
Lieutenant Governor
e: Detailed Explanation: Following the transfer of power from the East India Company to the Crown under the Act of 1858, the Governor-General was given the additional title of Viceroy to emphasize his status as the direct imperial representative of the British monarch in India.

qe: The Royal Commission on Decentralization (1908) recommended specific educational divisions for urban municipalities. Which tier of education did it suggest they should completely undertake?
qh: रॉयल कमीशन ऑन विकेंद्रीकरण (1908) ने शहरी नगर पालिकाओं के लिए विशिष्ट शैक्षिक प्रभागों की सिफारिश की थी। इसने शिक्षा के किस स्तर को पूरी तरह से संभालने का सुझाव दिया?
o: Primary education and, if willing, middle vernacular schools
Advanced technical research and power-generation scientific training
High-cost English-medium university courses exclusively
The management of specialized in-vitro medical institutions
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1908 Decentralization Commission recommended that urban municipalities should explicitly take up the financial and administrative responsibility for primary education and, if willing, middle vernacular schools, while being relieved of charges for higher secondary schools.

qe: The Regulating Act of 1773 was a watershed moment in British colonial history. What fundamental element did it introduce into the governance of the East India Company's territories?
qh: 1773 का रेगुलेटिंग एक्ट ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक इतिहास में एक महत्वपूर्ण मोड़ था। इसने ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी के क्षेत्रों के शासन में कौन सा मौलिक तत्व पेश किया?
o: The element of centralized administration
Absolute independent provincial autonomy
A uniform universal adult franchise tracking system
The complete permanent legal abolition of the Court of Directors
e: Detailed Explanation: The Regulating Act of 1773 brought about the British government’s involvement in Indian affairs to control and regulate the East India Company. It recognized that the Company’s role extended to administrative and political fields, and formally introduced the element of centralized administration.

qe: Under the provisions of the 1773 Regulating Act, the administration of Bengal was to be carried out by a Governor-General and a council. How many members composed this executive council?
qh: 1773 के रेगुलेटिंग एक्ट के प्रावधानों के तहत, बंगाल का प्रशासन एक गवर्नर-जनरल और एक परिषद द्वारा किया जाना था। इस कार्यकारी परिषद में कितने सदस्य शामिल थे?
o: 4 members
3 members
15 members
6 members
e: Detailed Explanation: The Act stipulated that the administration in Bengal would be conducted by a Governor-General and a council consisting of 4 members, representing the civil and military government. They were legally required to function according to majority rule.

qe: The Regulating Act of 1773 provided for the establishment of a Supreme Court of judicature in Bengal. What major structural problem arose from its practical operation?
qh: 1773 के रेगुलेटिंग एक्ट में बंगाल में एक सुप्रीम कोर्ट की स्थापना का प्रावधान था। इसके व्यावहारिक संचालन से कौन सी बड़ी संरचनात्मक समस्या उत्पन्न हुई?
o: The Supreme Court had a vague, debatable jurisdiction vis-a-vis the executive council
The court was completely barred from hearing any civil or military appeals
The judicial bench was financially subordinated to the local village punchayats
The absolute requirement that all judgments must be cleared by the native princes first
e: Detailed Explanation: Although a Supreme Court with original and appellate jurisdictions was established so that all subjects could seek redressal, in practice, it had a highly debatable jurisdiction vis-a-vis the Governor-General's council, creating various constitutional friction points.

qe: The Amending Act of 1781 was enacted to rectify the anomalies of the 1773 legislation. What judicial guideline did it establish for the Supreme Court within Calcutta?
qh: 1781 का संशोधन अधिनियम (Amending Act of 1781) 1773 के कानून की विसंगतियों को दूर करने के लिए अधिनियमित किया गया था। इसने कलकत्ता के भीतर सुप्रीम कोर्ट के लिए कौन सा विधायी दिशानिर्देश स्थापित किया?
o: It was defined to administer the personal law of the defendant
The court was stripped of any original jurisdiction over European subjects
It mandated that all judicial proceedings must be conducted in classical Sanskrit loops
The total legal abolition of any appellate jurisdictions regarding revenue administration
e: Detailed Explanation: The Amending Act of 1781 defined the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, stipulating that within Calcutta, it was bound to administer the personal law of the defendant. It also immunised government servants for actions done in the discharge of their official duties.

qe: Which landmark British legislation transformed the East India Company into a subordinate department of the State and officially termed the Company’s territories as 'British possessions'?
qh: किस ऐतिहासिक ब्रिटिश कानून ने ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी को राज्य के एक अधीनस्थ विभाग में बदल दिया और आधिकारिक तौर पर कंपनी के क्षेत्रों को 'ब्रिटिश संपत्ति' (British possessions) कहा?
o: Pitt’s India Act of 1784
The Regulating Act of 1773
The Charter Act of 1793
The Government of India Act, 1858
e: Detailed Explanation: Pitt’s India Act of 1784 gave the British government a large measure of control over the Company’s affairs, making the Company a subordinate department of the State. For the first time, the Company’s territories in India were officially termed 'British possessions'.

qe: Pitt’s India Act of 1784 established a dual system of control in England. Which body was constituted by the Crown to exercise control over the Company’s civil, military, and revenue affairs?
qh: 1784 के पिट्स इंडिया एक्ट ने इंग्लैंड में नियंत्रण की एक दोहरी प्रणाली स्थापित की। कंपनी के नागरिक, सैन्य और राजस्व मामलों पर नियंत्रण रखने के लिए क्राउन द्वारा किस निकाय का गठन किया गया था?
o: A Board of Control
The Court of Directors
The Indian Legislative Council
The Secretary of State's Advisory Panel
e: Detailed Explanation: Pitt's India Act set up a dual system of control. A new body called the Board of Control—consisting of the chancellor of the exchequer, a secretary of state, and four members of the Privy Council appointed by the Crown—was created to supervise civil, military, and revenue affairs.

qe: Under the structural modifications introduced by Pitt’s India Act of 1784, how was the composition of the Governor-General's council altered inside India?
qh: 1784 के पिट्स इंडिया एक्ट द्वारा शुरू किए गए संरचनात्मक संशोधनों के तहत, भारत के भीतर गवर्नर-जनरल की परिषद की संरचना को कैसे बदला गया था?
o: The council was reduced to three members, including the commander-in-chief
The council was expanded to include fifteen non-official nominated members
The executive councillors were made fully responsible to the provincial legislatures
The absolute structural separation of the revenue portfolio from civil administration
e: Detailed Explanation: In India, Pitt's India Act modified the executive machinery by reducing the Governor-General’s council from four members down to three (which explicitly included the commander-in-chief). It also made the presidencies of Bombay and Madras subordinate to the Governor-General.

qe: The specialized Act of 1786 was passed by the British Parliament to concede the specific administrative demands of which incoming Governor-General?
qh: ब्रिटिश संसद द्वारा किस नए गवर्नर-जनरल की विशिष्ट प्रशासनिक मांगों को स्वीकार करने के लिए 1786 का विशेष अधिनियम पारित किया गया था?
o: Lord Cornwallis
Warren Hastings
Lord Wellesley
Lord William Bentinck
e: Detailed Explanation: Lord Cornwallis demanded that he be given the powers of both the Governor-General and the Commander-in-Chief before taking office. The Act of 1786 conceded this demand and also gave him the extraordinary power to override the council's decision if he personally owned the responsibility for it.

qe: The Charter Act of 1793 introduced a controversial financial provision regarding the home government. Out of which funds were the members of the Board of Control to be paid?
qh: 1793 के चार्टर एक्ट ने गृह सरकार के संबंध में एक विवादास्पद वित्तीय प्रावधान पेश किया। बोर्ड ऑफ कंट्रोल के सदस्यों को किस फंड से भुगतान किया जाना था?
o: Indian revenues
The British Exchequer
The corporate profits of the London trade guild
A flat custom tax surcharge collected at European ports
e: Detailed Explanation: The Charter Act of 1793 mandated that the members of the Board of Control and the home government establishment were to be paid directly out of Indian revenues. This practice, heavily criticized as a drain of wealth, continued systematically all the way up to 1919.

qe: What structural reform did the Charter Act of 1793 execute regarding judicial administration that led to the disappearance of the traditional 'Maal Adalats'?
qh: 1793 के चार्टर एक्ट ने न्यायिक प्रशासन के संबंध में कौन सा संरचनात्मक सुधार लागू किया जिसके कारण पारंपरिक 'माल अदालतों' (Maal Adalats) का लोप हो गया?
o: The revenue administration was separated from the judiciary functions
The complete administrative subordination of all civil courts to the Zamindars
The mandatory introduction of competitive examinations to select district judges
The direct physical absorption of appellate jurisdictions by the Board of Control
e: Detailed Explanation: The Charter Act of 1793 introduced a key separation of functions by separating the revenue administration from judicial duties. This structural re-mapping directly led to the total disappearance of the Maal Adalats (revenue courts).

qe: The Charter Act of 1793 empowered the East India Company to give licenses to individuals and its own employees to trade in India. What was this trade popularly called, which paved the way for opium shipments to China?
qh: 1793 के चार्टर एक्ट ने ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी को व्यक्तियों और अपने स्वयं के कर्मचारियों को भारत में व्यापार करने के लिए लाइसेंस देने का अधिकार दिया। इस व्यापार को लोकप्रिय रूप से क्या कहा जाता था, जिसने चीन को अफीम के शिपमेंट का रास्ता साफ किया?
o: 'Privilege' or 'country trade'
The Free-float Laissez-faire framework
The Continental Transit system
The Regulated Imperial monopoly exchange
e: Detailed Explanation: The licenses granted under the 1793 Act were commercially known as 'privilege' or 'country trade'. This legal mechanism commercialized private trade loops and directly paved the way for the massive shipments of opium to China.

qe: The Charter Act of 1813 brought a major shift in British commercial policy by terminating the East India Company's trade monopoly in India. Which two specific trade areas were exclusively retained by the Company?
qh: 1813 के चार्टर एक्ट ने भारत में ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी के व्यापारिक एकाधिकार को समाप्त करके ब्रिटिश व्यावसायिक नीति में एक बड़ा बदलाव लाया। कंपनी द्वारा विशेष रूप से कौन से दो व्यापारिक क्षेत्र सुरक्षित रखे गए थे?
o: The trade with China and the trade in tea
The raw cotton export routes and opium shipments
The salt manufacturing monopoly and textile distribution
The maritime shipping lanes crossing the Malabar coast exclusively
e: Detailed Explanation: Driven by the spirit of laissez-faire and Napoleon's continental system blockades, the British Parliament ended the Company's trade monopoly in India via the 1813 Act. However, the Company successfully retained its exclusive monopoly over the trade with China and the trade in tea.

qe: Why do constitutional historians emphasize that the Charter Act of 1813 defined the constitutional position of British territories in India explicitly for the very first time?
qh: संवैधानिक इतिहासकार इस बात पर क्यों जोर देते हैं कि 1813 के चार्टर एक्ट ने पहली बार भारत में ब्रिटिश क्षेत्रों की संवैधानिक स्थिति को स्पष्ट रूप से परिभाषित किया था?
o: It declared that the Company was to retain possession of territories and revenues without prejudice to the sovereignty of the Crown
It formally dissolved the Board of Control and transferred all authority to popular ministries
It introduced a uniform legal code that granted universal adult franchise to all native ryots
It completely integrated the administrative boundaries of India with the Kingdom of Nepal
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1813 Act explicitly defined the constitutional status of British India by stating that while the Company would retain possession of the territories and local revenues for another 20 years, this was strictly 'without prejudice to the sovereignty of the Crown'.

qe: The Charter Act of 1813 incorporated a historic financial provision of one lakh rupees annually. For what specific public responsibility was this fund set aside?
qh: 1813 के चार्टर एक्ट में सालाना एक लाख रुपये का ऐतिहासिक वित्तीय प्रावधान शामिल था। यह फंड किस विशिष्ट सार्वजनिक जिम्मेदारी के लिए अलग रखा गया था?
o: The revival, promotion, and encouragement of literature, learning, and science among the natives
The direct corporate modernization of the arms stored inside British arsenals
Providing baseline cash revenue remissions to small agrarian peasants during droughts
Funding the logistical transport routes of the Christian missionaries inside Madras
e: Detailed Explanation: The Charter Act of 1813 stipulated that a sum of one lakh rupees would be set aside every year for the revival, promotion, and encouragement of literature, learning, and science among the natives of India. This marked the first formal recognition of the State's responsibility for education.

qe: Which religious group was officially permitted to enter India and preach their faith for the first time under the statutory provisions of the Charter Act of 1813?
qh: 1813 के चार्टर एक्ट के वैधानिक प्रावधानों के तहत पहली बार किस धार्मिक समूह को भारत में प्रवेश करने और अपने धर्म का प्रचार करने की आधिकारिक अनुमति दी गई थी?
o: Christian missionaries
The orthodox ulema of the Deoband School
The high-caste Hindu reformation sadhus
The Parsi spiritual advisory councils
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1813 Act opened the doors to socio-religious interventions by explicitly permitting Christian missionaries to come to India, travel freely, and preach their religion across the territories.

qe: The Charter Act of 1833 executed a sweeping commercial change that finalized the conversion of the East India Company into a purely administrative body. What was this change?
qh: 1833 के चार्टर एक्ट ने एक व्यापक व्यावसायिक परिवर्तन लागू किया जिसने ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी को पूरी तरह से एक प्रशासनिक निकाय में बदलने का काम पूरा किया। यह बदलाव क्या था?
o: The Company’s monopoly over trade with China and in tea was completely ended
The complete physical liquidation of all assets held by the Court of Directors in London
The mandatory financial subordination of the Board of Control to the popular Indian ministers
Forcing the Company to transfer 100% of its textile factories to native Indian capitalists
e: Detailed Explanation: The Charter Act of 1833 completely stripped the East India Company of its remaining commercial character by permanently ending its lucrative monopoly over the trade with China and in tea, turning it into a purely political and administrative trust governing in the name of the Crown.

qe: What drastic legislative restriction was imposed on the regional Presidencies of Bombay and Madras by the extreme centralizing parameters of the Charter Act of 1833?
qh: 1833 के चार्टर एक्ट के अत्यधिक केंद्रीकरण मापदंडों द्वारा बॉम्बे और मद्रास की क्षेत्रीय प्रेसीडेंसियों पर कौन सा कड़ा विधायी प्रतिबंध लगाया गया था?
o: They were drastically deprived of their independent legislative powers, leaving them only a right to propose law projects
They were completely merged into a single coastal administrative zone directed by the Mayor's court
They were given absolute sovereign veto powers to override any central financial allocations
They were legally forced to conduct all their official administrative proceedings in classical Latin codes
e: Detailed Explanation: To achieve complete centralization, the 1833 Act placed all territories under the absolute control of the Governor-General. It drastically deprived the Governments of Madras and Bombay of their independent legislative powers, leaving them merely with the right to propose draft projects of law to the center.

qe: To provide specialized professional advice during the expanded legislative drafting phases, what new member was added to the Governor-General’s council under the 1933 Act?
qh: विस्तारित विधायी प्रारूपण चरणों के दौरान विशेष पेशेवर सलाह प्रदान करने के लिए, 1833 के अधिनियम के तहत गवर्नर-जनरल की परिषद में कौन सा नया सदस्य जोड़ा गया था?
o: A law member
A finance specialist councillor
A permanent representative chosen by the native princes
The Chief Justice of the newly constituted central Circuit Court
e: Detailed Explanation: The Charter Act of 1833 modified the executive council's structure by adding a fourth member, a specialized 'law member', to provide professional advice on law-making and oversee the codification of Indian laws.

qe: Which famous statutory declaration within the Charter Act of 1833—stating that no citizen could be denied employment under the Company based on religion, color, or birth—served as the sheet-anchor for future political agitations?
qh: 1833 के चार्टर एक्ट के भीतर कौन सी प्रसिद्ध वैधानिक घोषणा - जिसमें कहा गया था कि किसी भी नागरिक को धर्म, रंग या जन्म के आधार पर कंपनी के तहत रोजगार से वंचित नहीं किया जा सकता - भविष्य के राजनीतिक आंदोलनों का मुख्य आधार बनी?
o: Section 87 clause regarding non-discriminatory employment
The absolute abolition of separate communal electorates framework
The mandatory implementation of universal adult franchise tracking charts
The charter clause transferring the high courts control directly to the legislature
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1833 Act contained a historic declaration stating that no Indian citizen would be denied employment under the Company on the basis of religion, color, birth, descent, or place of birth. Although unfulfilled in reality, this declaration became the sheet-anchor of modern political agitations in India.

qe: Following the explicit humanitarian urgings of the Charter Act of 1833 to ameliorate the conditions of bound laborers, in which year was slavery officially and completely abolished in British India?
qh: बंधुआ मजदूरों की स्थिति में सुधार के लिए 1833 के चार्टर एक्ट के स्पष्ट मानवीय आग्रहों के बाद, ब्रिटिश भारत में किस वर्ष दासता (slavery) को आधिकारिक और पूरी तरह से समाप्त कर दिया गया था?
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1833 Act urged the central administration to take active steps to ameliorate the conditions of slaves and ultimately abolish slavery. Following these directives, slavery was formally and legally abolished in British India in the year 1843.

qe: The Charter Act of 1853 introduced a fundamental shift in the recruitment of civil servants by breaking the traditional patronage network. How were the services now thrown open to applicants?
qh: 1853 के चार्टर एक्ट ने पारंपरिक संरक्षण नेटवर्क को तोड़कर सिविल सेवकों की भर्ती में एक मौलिक बदलाव पेश किया। अब आवेदकों के लिए सेवाएं किस प्रकार खोली गईं?
o: The services were thrown open to a system of open competitive examinations
The seats were reserved exclusively to be nominated by the native Princely rulers
The recruitment was handled directly by the executive committees of the village panchayats
The positions were sold via public auctions to the highest bidding urban landlords
e: Detailed Explanation: The Charter Act of 1853 dissolved the Company’s traditional patronage over the civil services. It introduced a progressive, transparent meritocracy by throwing the superior services open to an open competitive examination system.

qe: What structural change occurred regarding the status of the 'law member' within the Governor-General’s Executive Council under the provisions of the 1853 Charter Act?
qh: 1853 के चार्टर एक्ट के प्रावधानों के तहत गवर्नर-जनरल की कार्यकारी परिषद के भीतर 'कानून सदस्य' (law member) की स्थिति के संबंध में क्या संरचनात्मक परिवर्तन हुआ था?
o: The law member became a full member of the executive council
The office of the law member was completely abolished and its portfolios dissolved
He was stripped of any voting rights and restricted strictly to an advisory role
The position was made directly answerable and removable by the adverse vote of the assembly
e: Detailed Explanation: Progressing from the framework established in 1833, the Charter Act of 1853 elevated the administrative status of the law member, making him a full, permanent member of the Governor-General’s Executive Council.

qe: The separation of the executive and legislative functions of the British Indian government progressed significantly under the 1853 Act. How many additional members were newly included for specific legislative purposes?
qh: 1853 के अधिनियम के तहत ब्रिटिश भारतीय सरकार के कार्यकारी और विधायी कार्यों का पृथक्करण महत्वपूर्ण रूप से आगे बढ़ा। विशिष्ट विधायी उद्देश्यों के लिए कितने अतिरिक्त सदस्य नए शामिल किए गए थे?
o: Six additional members
Fourteen members
Fifteen members
Exactly three members
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1853 Act marked a distinct transition toward separating powers by expanding the Governor-General's council for legislative purposes through the inclusion of exactly six additional members.

qe: The expanded legislative wing established under the Charter Act of 1853 introduced local representation and became historically known as the:
qh: 1853 के चार्टर एक्ट के तहत स्थापित विस्तारित विधायी विंग ने स्थानीय प्रतिनिधित्व की शुरुआत की और इसे ऐतिहासिक रूप से किस नाम से जाना गया?
o: Indian Legislative Council
Board of Control Assembly
Constituent Assembly of India
Swarajya Sabha Parliamentary Front
e: Detailed Explanation: The inclusion of the additional legislative members and local representation under the 1853 Act transformed the legislative wing, which officially came to be designated as the Indian Legislative Council.

qe: Despite creating a dedicated Indian Legislative Council in 1853, what absolute constitutional restriction maintained the Governor-General's autocratic dominance over legislation?
qh: 1853 में एक समर्पित भारतीय विधान परिषद बनाने के बावजूद, किस पूर्ण संवैधानिक प्रतिबंध ने कानून पर गवर्नर-जनरल के निरंकुश वर्चस्व को बनाए रखा?
o: A law to be promulgated required his assent, and he could veto any Bill of the legislative council
He held the sovereign power to permanently arrest any non-official legislator without trial
The Governor-General could independently alter the provincial list boundaries without legislative voting
He was legally authorized to dissolve the British Parliament in London during legislative deadlocks
e: Detailed Explanation: The Indian Legislative Council was not a sovereign body. To promulgate any piece of legislation, the explicit assent of the Governor-General was mandatory, and he was armed with absolute powers to veto any Bill passed by the council.

qe: The historic 'Act for Better Government of India, 1858' was passed following the 1857 revolt. Through which specialized administrative position was India to be governed henceforth in the name of the Crown?
qh: 1857 के विद्रोह के बाद ऐतिहासिक 'Act for Better Government of India, 1858' पारित किया गया था। अब से किस विशेष प्रशासनिक पद के माध्यम से भारत पर क्राउन के नाम से शासन किया जाना था?
o: A Secretary of State for India accompanied by a council of 15
The President of the Board of Control operating through separate secret tools
A High Commissioner based in London holding a six-year tenure
The Chief Justice of the central Sadar Diwani Adalat in Calcutta
e: Detailed Explanation: Enacted to rectify the lack of accountability exposed by the 1857 uprising, the 1858 Act transferred governance to the British Crown. It established that India would be governed by and in the name of the Crown through a Secretary of State for India, assisted by an advisory council of 15 members.

qe: The enactment of the Act for Better Government of India, 1858, brought a decisive end to which complex administrative mechanism that had been in place since 1784?
qh: 1858 के भारत सरकार अधिनियम के अधिनियमन ने किस जटिल प्रशासनिक तंत्र का निर्णायक अंत कर दिया जो 1784 से लागू था?
o: The dual system of control introduced by Pitt’s India Act
The centralized administration scheme designed by Warren Hastings
The separate accounts tracking system managed by Maal Adalats
The commercial trade monopoly over China and the trade in tea
e: Detailed Explanation: Because the initiative and final decision-making power were concentrated solely in the hands of the Secretary of State, the 1858 Act formally brought a decisive end to the dual system of control originally set up by Pitt’s India Act of 1784.

qe: What high-prestige title was appended to the office of the Governor-General under the provisions of the 1858 Act, reflecting his position as the direct representative of the Crown?
qh: 1858 के अधिनियम के प्रावधानों के तहत गवर्नर-जनरल के पद के साथ कौन सा उच्च-प्रतिष्ठा वाला शीर्षक जोड़ा गया था, जो क्राउन के सीधे प्रतिनिधि के रूप में उनकी स्थिति को दर्शाता है?
o: Viceroy
Premier
High Commissioner
Chancellor of the Exchequer
e: Detailed Explanation: Following the formal assumption of power by the British Crown, the Governor-General was additionally designated as the Viceroy of India, which significantly elevated his prestige and symbolic status across the sub-continent.

qe: The Indian Councils Act of 1861 marked a progressive milestone by formally accepting which baseline principle regarding the composition of legislative bodies?
qh: 1861 के भारतीय परिषद अधिनियम ने विधायी निकायों की संरचना के संबंध में किस बुनियादी सिद्धांत को औपचारिक रूप से स्वीकार करके एक प्रगतिशील मील का पत्थर स्थापित किया?
o: The principle of representation of non-officials in legislative bodies
The immediate and complete introduction of universal adult suffrage across all districts
The mandatory selection of all council members via open competitive military test loops
Restricting the entry of legislators exclusively to the landless agricultural untouchables
e: Detailed Explanation: The Indian Councils Act of 1861 marked an advance by formally accepting the principle of non-official representation inside the legislative bodies, ensuring that laws were made after due deliberation rather than being the exclusive business of the executive.

qe: Which innovative administrative mechanism introduced by Lord Canning was validated by the Indian Councils Act of 1861, laying the solid foundations of cabinet government in India?
qh: लॉर्ड कैनिंग द्वारा शुरू किए गए किस अभिनव प्रशासनिक तंत्र को 1861 के भारतीय परिषद अधिनियम द्वारा मान्यता दी गई थी, जिसने भारत में कैबिनेट सरकार की मजबूत नींव रखी?
o: The portfolio system
The dual control system
The Maal Adalat grid
The separate accounts registry framework
e: Detailed Explanation: Lord Canning introduced the 'portfolio system', where each branch of the administration had its official head and spokesman responsible for its performance. The 1861 Act validated this system, laying the structural foundations of cabinet government in India.

qe: How did the Indian Councils Act of 1861 lay the structural foundations of legislative devolution across British India?
qh: 1861 के भारतीय परिषद अधिनियम ने ब्रिटिश भारत में विधायी हस्तांतरण (legislative devolution) की संरचनात्मक नींव कैसे रखी?
o: By vesting independent legislative powers back in the Governments of Bombay and Madras and providing for similar councils in other provinces
By completely transferring the absolute central customs revenues to local municipalities directly
By legally forcing the central legislature to accept the sovereign veto power of popular premiums
The total administrative integration of all provincial list boundaries under a single military Governor
e: Detailed Explanation: Reversing the extreme centralization of 1833, the 1861 Act restored legislative powers to the Governments of Bombay and Madras. By making provisions to institute similar legislative councils in other provinces, it successfully laid the foundations of legislative devolution.

qe: Despite introducing legislative councils, the Indian Councils Act of 1861 left them crippled with severe weaknesses. Which of the following highlights a limitation faced by these councils?
qh: विधान परिषदों की शुरुआत करने के बावजूद, 1861 के भारतीय परिषद अधिनियम ने उन्हें गंभीर कमजोरियों के साथ छोड़ दिया। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा इन परिषदों द्वारा सामना की जाने वाली एक सीमा को रेखांकित करता है?
o: They could not discuss important matters or any financial matters at all without the previous approval of the government, and held zero control over the budget
They were legally forced to pass all their legislative bills within a strict 24-hour emergency window
The members were chosen via an open universal franchise that completely excluded the elite sections
They were financially dependent on the personal capital grant donations of the Forward Bloc
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1861 councils possessed no real power. They were strictly barred from discussing important matters or any financial portfolios without previous official approval, held no control over the budget, could not check executive actions, and their bills could be disallowed by the Secretary of State even after Viceroy approval.

qe: Following its foundation in 1885, the Indian National Congress aggressively demanded council reforms as the 'root of all other reforms'. How did the colonial state respond through the Indian Councils Act of 1892?
qh: 1885 में अपनी स्थापना के बाद, भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस ने काउंसिल सुधारों को 'अन्य सभी सुधारों की जड़' के रूप में आक्रामक रूप से मांगा। औपनिवेशिक राज्य ने 1892 के भारतीय परिषद अधिनियम के माध्यम से कैसी प्रतिक्रिया दी?
o: The number of non-official members was increased both in the central (Imperial) and provincial legislative councils
The state completely dissolved the Indian Legislative Council to establish a military dictatorship
They passed a law restricting council seats exclusively to the members of the Landholders' Society
They introduced a separate electorate framework for all intermediate non-Brahmin caste groups
e: Detailed Explanation: In direct response to the political pressure and demands generated by the newly founded Indian National Congress, the British Parliament passed the Indian Councils Act of 1892, which structurally increased the number of non-official members in both the central (Imperial) and provincial legislative councils.

qe: The Indian Councils Act of 1892 introduced a pioneering mechanism by empowering certain local bodies to recommend members to the provincial councils. What principle did this establish?
qh: 1892 के भारतीय परिषद अधिनियम ने प्रांतीय परिषदों में सदस्यों की सिफारिश करने के लिए कुछ स्थानीय निकायों को सशक्त बनाकर एक अग्रणी तंत्र पेश किया। इससे कौन सा सिद्धांत स्थापित हुआ?
o: The principle of representation
Universal adult franchise tracking
The complete isolation of the executive
Sovereign legislative responsibility
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1892 Act authorized elite local bodies—including universities, district boards, municipalities, zamindars, and chambers of commerce—to recommend names for council nominations, thereby introducing the vital principle of representation into the political process.

qe: Although the term 'election' was firmly avoided in the text of the Indian Councils Act of 1892, what innovative electoral element was practically accepted in the selection of non-official members?
qh: हालाँकि 1892 के भारतीय परिषद अधिनियम के पाठ में 'चुनाव' (election) शब्द से दृढ़ता से बचा गया था, लेकिन गैर-आधिकारिक सदस्यों के चयन में व्यावहारिक रूप से कौन सा अभिनव चुनावी तत्व स्वीकार किया गया था?
o: An element of indirect election
An open direct universal adult suffrage framework
A competitive structural testing evaluation loop in English
Absolute random lottery selection managed by the Viceroy
e: Detailed Explanation: To counter radical demands while updating the system, the 1892 Act avoided using the word 'election' in its text but practically accepted an element of indirect election through the recommendation process of local commercial and educational bodies.

qe: What new operational privilege did the members of the legislatures acquire regarding public finance under the provisions of the Indian Councils Act of 1892?
qh: 1892 के भारतीय परिषद अधिनियम के प्रावधानों के तहत विधानसभाओं के सदस्यों ने सार्वजनिक वित्त के संबंध में कौन सा नया परिचालन विशेषाधिकार प्राप्त किया था?
o: They were entitled to express their views upon financial statements made on the floor of the legislatures
They were armed with absolute sovereign veto powers to completely reject the annual imperial budget
They could independently reallocate 50% of the revenue shares to support national schools
They were authorized to audit the personal home charges expenditures of the Secretary of State
e: Detailed Explanation: Expanding the deliberative powers of the legislatures, the 1892 Act statutorily entitled members to express their views and debate the annual financial statements (budget) presented on the floor of the house.

qe: Under the modified questioning guidelines of the 1892 Act, members could put questions to the executive on matters of public interest. What timeframe notice was mandatory before asking a question?
qh: 1892 के अधिनियम के संशोधित प्रश्न पूछने के दिशानिर्देशों के तहत, सदस्य जनहित के मामलों पर कार्यपालिका से प्रश्न पूछ सकते थे। प्रश्न पूछने से पहले कितनी समय-सीमा का नोटिस देना अनिवार्य था?
o: Six days’ notice
A strict 24-hour notice
A two-week formal registry window
No notice was required under the new rules
e: Detailed Explanation: The Indian Councils Act of 1892 permitted legislators to ask questions to the executive branch on matters of public interest, subject to certain limits and the mandatory submission of a six days’ prior notice.

qe: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 is popularly known by which alternative nomenclature in modern Indian history?
qh: भारतीय परिषद अधिनियम, 1909 को आधुनिक भारतीय इतिहास में किस वैकल्पिक नाम से जाना जाता है?
o: Morley-Minto Reforms
Montague-Chelmsford Reforms
The Pitt’s India structural updates
The Cornwallis Code revisions chart
e: Detailed Explanation: The Indian Councils Act of 1909, which made the first formal attempt to introduce a representative and popular element into governance, is widely known as the Morley-Minto Reforms.

qe: Who holds the historic distinction of being appointed as the very first Indian member to the Governor-General’s Executive Council in 1909 under the provisions of the Morley-Minto Reforms?
qh: लॉरेंस-मिंटो सुधारों के प्रावधानों के तहत 1909 में गवर्नर-जनरल की कार्यकारी परिषद (Executive Council) में नियुक्त होने वाले पहले भारतीय सदस्य होने का ऐतिहासिक गौरव किसे प्राप्त है?
o: Satyendra Prasad Sinha
Rashbehari Ghosh
Gopal Krishna Gokhale
Ananda Mohan Bose
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1909 Act introduced an important structural change by admitting an Indian member into the Viceroy's executive core for the first time. Satyendra Prasad Sinha was appointed to this high seat, serving as the Law Member.

qe: Despite expanding the councils, what remained the primary limitation of the 1909 Morley-Minto framework regarding the actual distribution of administrative power?
qh: परिषदों का विस्तार करने के बावजूद, प्रशासनिक शक्ति के वास्तविक वितरण के संबंध में 1909 के मॉर्ले-मिंटो ढांचे की प्राथमिक सीमा क्या बनी रही?
o: The real power remained with the government, and the councils were left with no functions but criticism
The lower assembly was granted an absolute veto power to summarily dismiss the Viceroy
The entire legislative machinery was completely dissolved in favor of direct military rule
The councils were financially dependent on the capital grant allocations of local panchayats
e: Detailed Explanation: The reforms did not alter the autocratic core of colonial rule. Real power remained concentrated entirely in the hands of the official executive, leaving the expanded councils with no sovereign functions but the power of criticism.

qe: Apart from separate electorates, what additional discriminatory electoral privileges were explicitly accorded to Muslim voters under the Indian Councils Act of 1909 layout?
qh: पृथक निर्वाचन मंडल के अलावा, भारतीय परिषद अधिनियम 1909 के खाके के तहत मुस्लिम मतदाताओं को कौन से अतिरिक्त भेदभावपूर्ण चुनावी विशेषाधिकार दिए गए थे?
o: Representation in excess of their population strength and lower income qualification thresholds than Hindus
The exclusive statutory right to vote on the entire annual budget of the central council
Complete legal exemption from paying any land revenue or salt taxes across the country
The dynamic right to issue religious decrees against British executive actions directly
