e: Detailed Explanation: To further colonial divide-and-rule tactics, the 1909 Act granted Muslims political representation in excess of their actual population percentage and kept the income qualification threshold for Muslim voters lower than that required for Hindu voters.

qe: The Government of India Act, 1919 was based on what popular constitutional reform nomenclature?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1919 किस लोकप्रिय संवैधानिक सुधार नामकरण (nomenclature) पर आधारित था?
o: Montague-Chelmsford Reforms
Morley-Minto Reforms
The Cornwallis administrative code
The Pitt's India dual system charts
e: Detailed Explanation: The Government of India Act of 1919, which introduced major structural re-mappings, was based on the proposals historically known as the Montague-Chelmsford Reforms.

qe: The British declaration of August 1917 stated that its objective was the gradual introduction of responsible government. How did the 1919 Act qualify this path, targeting Indian demands for self-determination?
qh: अगस्त 1917 की ब्रिटिश घोषणा में कहा गया था कि इसका उद्देश्य क्रमिक रूप से जिम्मेदार सरकार की शुरुआत करना था। 1919 के अधिनियम ने आत्मनिर्भरता की भारतीय मांगों को निशाना बनाते हुए इस मार्ग को कैसे योग्य बनाया?
o: It clarified that the British Parliament—and not self-determination of the people—would determine the time and manner of each step
It granted immediate absolute sovereignty to the people to draft their own constitution via a constituent assembly
It completely integrated all central legislative functions under a joint council of the popular premiums
It made any constitutional progress strictly dependent on the financial clearances of the princely rulers
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1919 Act firmly restricted Indian aspirations by clarifying that there would only be a gradual development of self-governing institutions and explicitly stated that the British Parliament—and under no circumstances the self-determination of the Indian people—would determine the time and manner of each constitutional step.

qe: Under the Government of India Act 1919, the unicameral Indian Legislative Council at the Centre was replaced by a bicameral system. What were the names of the two newly created houses?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1919 के तहत, केंद्र में एकसदनीय भारतीय विधान परिषद के स्थान पर एक द्विसदनीय व्यवस्था लागू की गई। नवसृजित दोनों सदनों के नाम क्या थे?
o: The Council of State and the Legislative Assembly
The Federal Assembly and the House of Representatives
The Senate and the Imperial Executive Council
The Chamber of Princes and the Provincial Board
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1919 Act introduced central bicameralism, replacing the older single chamber with a two-house parliament: an upper house named the Council of State and a lower house named the Legislative Assembly.

qe: The Government of India Act, 1919 further extended the principle of communal representation. Which of the following sets of groups was awarded separate electorates alongside Muslims?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1919 ने सांप्रदायिक प्रतिनिधित्व के सिद्धांत का और विस्तार किया। मुसलमानों के साथ-साथ निम्नलिखित में से किस समूह को अलग निर्वाचन क्षेत्र दिया गया था?
o: Sikhs, Christians, and Anglo-Indians
Parsis, Jews, and Buddhists exclusively
The intermediate non-Brahmin landless untouchable laborers
The wealthy urban zamindars of the Permanent Settlement zones
e: Detailed Explanation: Deepening communal divisions, the 1919 reforms extended separate communal electorates to include three new minority classifications alongside the existing Muslim block: the Sikhs, Indian Christians, and Anglo-Indians.

qe: What major structural system did the 1919 Act introduce within the provincial administrative sector, spliting portfolios into two distinct categories?
qh: 1919 के अधिनियम ने प्रांतीय प्रशासनिक क्षेत्र के भीतर कौन सी प्रमुख संरचनात्मक प्रणाली शुरू की, जिसने विभागों को दो अलग-अलग श्रेणियों में विभाजित किया?
o: Dyarchy
Provincial Autonomy
Bicameralism
Saptanga Sovereignty
e: Detailed Explanation: The Government of India Act of 1919 introduced the system of 'Dyarchy' (dual rule) in the provinces, splitting portfolios into reserved and transferred lists, which marked an intermediate step toward power devolution.

qe: The 1919 Act introduced a major fiscal reform by separating central and provincial budgets for the first time. What new power did this award to the provincial legislatures?
qh: 1919 के अधिनियम ने पहली बार केंद्रीय और प्रांतीय बजट को अलग करके एक बड़ा वित्तीय सुधार पेश किया। इसने प्रांतीय विधानसभाओं को कौन सी नई शक्ति दी?
o: They were authorized to make their own budgets independent of the center
They could completely veto the financial allocations of the central Legislative Assembly
They were legally empowered to print independent provincial paper currencies
They held the absolute right to audit the home charges accounts of London treasury
e: Detailed Explanation: Achieving financial demarcation, the 1919 Act separated the provincial and central budgets for the first time, formally authorizing the provincial legislatures to frame and enact their own independent budgets.

qe: A high-profile diplomatic position was established in London under the 1919 Act to look after Indian trade in Europe for a six-year tenure. What was this office called?
qh: यूरोप में भारतीय व्यापार की देखरेख के लिए 1919 के अधिनियम के तहत लंदन में छह साल के कार्यकाल के लिए एक हाई-प्रोफाइल राजनयिक पद स्थापित किया गया था। इस कार्यालय को क्या कहा जाता था?
o: High Commissioner for India
Secretary of State for Indian Commerce
Viceroy's Imperial Envoy
Chancellor of the Trade Guild
e: Detailed Explanation: The Act of 1919 provided for the appointment of a High Commissioner for India based in London for a fixed six-year tenure to look after Indian commercial interests in Europe, absorbing some duties previously managed by the Secretary of State.

qe: The Government of India Act 1919 undid a long-standing financial injustice originally introduced by the Charter Act of 1793. What was this corrective measure?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1919 ने मूल रूप से 1793 के चार्टर अधिनियम द्वारा शुरू किए गए एक लंबे समय से चले आ रहे वित्तीय अन्याय को दूर किया। यह सुधारात्मक कदम क्या था?
o: The Secretary of State for India was henceforth to be paid by the British Exchequer instead of Indian revenues
The total legal abolition of the Maal Adalats and revenue courts across all presidencies
The direct transfer of the collected capital inputs of the Tilak Swaraj Fund to local bodies
An absolute reduction of the land revenue tax assessments down to a flat zero threshold
e: Detailed Explanation: Reversing an exploitative fiscal policy from 1793, the 1919 Act stipulated that the Secretary of State for India would henceforth receive his salary and administrative maintenance from the British Exchequer rather than drawing it from Indian tax revenues.

qe: According to the constitutional observations of Subhash Kashyap, what was the actual legal character of the central Indian legislature under the 1919 Act framework?
qh: सुभाष कश्यप के संवैधानिक आकलनों के अनुसार, 1919 के अधिनियम के ढांचे के तहत मध्य भारतीय विधायिका का वास्तविक कानूनी चरित्र क्या था?
o: It was only a non-sovereign law-making body and was powerless before the executive in all spheres
It functioned as an absolute sovereign constituent assembly equipped with supreme veto powers
It was a completely independent body that held full administrative control over the higher judiciary
It operated as a minor advisory board whose decisions had to be cleared by the village panchayats
e: Detailed Explanation: As noted by Subhash Kashyap, despite possessing the power to vote supplies and being more representative, the central legislature under the 1919 Act remained a non-sovereign law-making body that was ultimately powerless before an autocratic executive, with its legislation subject to the overriding vetoes and certification powers of the Governor-General.
